advances: In the zero-same-body-interaction part of the positive cap-synchronized overlap branch, the overlap submatching has a dimension-free macroscopic transverse pairing after the already accepted large-core alternative is removed.  The pairing splits exactly according to equality or inequality of the common stress contact and the chosen cap contact.  Equality gives cap-aligned affine stress squares; inequality gives genuine nonseparable cap-versus-stress squares.  Each reservoir also supplies separate, legal residual-selector, off-diagonal-centroid, and reflected-cloud certificates.  No energies from different squares or charts are added.
author: research-agent
proof:
Accepted fact 179add32aa016da1 gives (3), or else (4) together with all of its synchronized conclusions.  We work in the latter case.  It also gives
\[
 \sum_{\xi\notin\mathcal G}A_\xi<4G
\tag{41}
\]
and, after this bad-parity loss has been removed, defines (7) with support entirely in \(\mathcal G\) and proves
\[
 S_i:=\sum_es_{i,e}>
 \frac{\gamma_d\eta^2}{8}W.
\tag{42}
\]
Thus the bad parity classes are accounted for before the overlap is formed; neither \(r\) nor any reservoir constructed from it has support in a bad class.  Accepted fact 695b44a4f0fdcd3a gives the exact clipped identity
\[
 S_i=\sum_e\min\{s_{i,e},\omega_e\}
      +\sum_e(s_{i,e}-\omega_e)_+
 =R+\sum_e(s_{i,e}-\omega_e)_+.
\tag{43}
\]
Its affine-retention alternative handles the second summand when it is macroscopic.  Hypothesis (11) is precisely the remaining positive-overlap branch.  Notice from (7) that
\[
 0\leq r_e\leq s_{i,e}\leq\frac12q_e^\times.
\tag{44}
\]

We prove the transverse extraction for these subweights rather than applying the full-load conclusion of accepted fact cacf8017a747fd4c without checking its scale.  The feasible set in (13)-(14) is a nonempty compact polytope, so an optimizer exists.  Put
\[
 \kappa_e:=
 \sum_{f:\{e,f\}\in\mathcal A_2(r)}
 \vartheta_{\{e,f\}},
 \qquad
 \zeta_e:=r_e-\kappa_e\geq0,
 \qquad
 L:=\sum_e\zeta_e.
\tag{45}
\]
Each pairing variable is charged to both of its source edges, hence
\[
 L=R-2P.
\tag{46}
\]
If two positive residual edges share a base endpoint and have linearly independent half-directions there, their pairing variable can be increased by a positive amount.  This contradicts optimality.  Therefore, at every base vertex, all incident positive-residual edge directions are pairwise dependent.  Propagation along an edge path, with reversal of direction at the other endpoint, shows that every connected component of the positive-residual graph is contained in one affine lattice line.  This is the same exact residual argument as in accepted fact cacf8017a747fd4c, now applied to \(r\).

We next redo its product-capacity estimate with the sharper subweight in (44).  A residual component lies in one good parity class \(\xi\).  Let its vertex set be \(V_{\xi,j}\), let
\[
 B_{\xi,j}:=\sum_{z\in V_{\xi,j}}a_z,
\]
and enumerate the pairwise vertex-disjoint residual components in that class by \(j\).  Since (2) gives \(G<W/4\), the affine-line estimate in accepted fact cacf8017a747fd4c gives
\[
 B_{\xi,j}\leq2^{3-n}G.
\tag{47}
\]
Using (6), (44), and \(\sum_jB_{\xi,j}\leq A_\xi\), we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sum_{\substack{e\subseteq\xi}}\zeta_e
 &\leq
 \sum_j\sum_{\{u,v\}\subseteq V_{\xi,j}}
       \frac12q^\times_{\{u,v\}}\\
 &=\frac{\gamma_d}{4A_\xi}
   \sum_j\left(B_{\xi,j}^2
          -\sum_{z\in V_{\xi,j}}a_z^2\right)\\
 &\leq\frac{\gamma_d}{4}
       \max_jB_{\xi,j}
 \leq\gamma_d2^{1-n}G.
\end{aligned}
\tag{48}
\]
There are at most \(2^n\) parity classes and \(\gamma_d\leq1/2\).  Summing (48) therefore gives
\[
 \boxed{L\leq2\gamma_dG\leq G.}
\tag{49}
\]
Equations (46) and (49) give the first inequality in (15).  Accepted fact 695b44a4f0fdcd3a records \(\gamma_d\geq e^{-1}\).  From (4) and (11),
\[
 \frac GR<\frac{4}{25\gamma_d}\leq\frac{4e}{25},
\tag{50}
\]
which gives the middle inequality in (15).  Directly using the two bounds on \(G\) and \(R\) gives
\[
 P\geq\frac{R-G}{2}
 >\frac12\left(\frac{\gamma_d\eta^2}{16}
                -\frac{\eta^2}{100}\right)W
 =\frac{25\gamma_d-4}{800}\eta^2W.
\tag{51}
\]
This proves (15).  Equations (18)-(19) follow by partitioning the optimizer according to its unique common endpoint.

Because \(R>0\), the stress has positive load.  Equation (9) and accepted fact dcccecd70b052857 imply that all stress contacts and normalized stress directions at a loaded endpoint collapse to \(x_z,u_z\).  The same accepted fact proves that every nonzero direction of \(\mathcal K_z\) has a unique support contact and every such contact has a unique nonzero outward-normal ray.  Since both \(u_z\) and \(\widehat w_{i,z}\) have support value one on \(D_z\), this proves (17).

For completeness, the exact cap-versus-stress gap is
\[
 g_{i,z}^{\mathrm{cap}}
 :=\langle u_z-\widehat w_{i,z},
             x_z-y_{i,z}\rangle
\tag{52}
\]
\[
 =\bigl(1-\langle u_z,y_{i,z}-c_z\rangle\bigr)
  +\bigl(1-\langle\widehat w_{i,z},x_z-c_z\rangle\bigr)
 \geq0.
\tag{53}
\]
Both terms are nonnegative support gaps.  Equality forces each cross contact to be a support contact in the other direction; contact uniqueness then gives \(x_z=y_{i,z}\).  Hence (52) is strictly positive exactly in the distinct-contact class.  No quantitative lower bound on this positive gap is used or claimed.

Fix a positive paired contribution and orient it as in (20).  Feasibility and (44) give
\[
 0<\theta_\sigma\leq r_e,r_f
 \leq\frac12q_e^\times,\frac12q_f^\times.
\tag{54}
\]
The endpoint degree bound for \(q^\times\) is
\[
 d_z(q^\times)\leq\gamma_da_z\leq\frac{a_z}{2}.
\tag{55}
\]
Thus every stress or cap contact used in (21) or (26), originally a half-mass metronoid point, can be represented at the smaller selected mass \(\theta_\sigma\) by scaling a half-mass witness.  The positive-root metronoid interpolation proved and used in accepted fact 1c54f5dc74c15059 then gives all midpoint memberships in (22) and (27).  The base half-directions are integral because the edges are same-parity, and they are independent by the definition of \(\mathcal A_2(r)\).  This proves that \(\Phi_\sigma\) is a legal rank-two integral chart.

For the stress square, zero interaction gives the same common contact \(x_z\) on both source edges, and direct cancellation gives (23).  In the equal-contact class, \(u_z=\widehat w_{i,z}\).  Each stress vector \(v_e^\times\), respectively \(v_f^\times\), lies on this positive ray.  At the opposite endpoint, its stress support contact is therefore the unique support contact in direction \(w_i\), proving (24).

For the cap-versus-stress square, direct cancellation gives (28), which is nonzero by classification.  Membership in a selected-mass metronoid implies absolute fiber depth at least \(\gamma_d\theta_\sigma\), by the depth input used in accepted fact 1c54f5dc74c15059.  Applying its constant two-by-two factor construction gives energies (25) and (29).  These applications are local, one contribution at a time.

We verify the asserted simultaneous source feasibility without summing target-fiber constructions.  Choose once a half-mass witness for every stress contact and every cap contact used above.  Scale a source witness in fiber \(C_y\) by \(2\theta_\sigma/a_y\) when it occurs in one outer point.  For any subfamily, the sum of occurrence weights at \(y\) is at most
\[
 \sum_{e\ni y}\kappa_e
 \leq d_y(r)
 \leq\frac12d_y(q^\times)
 \leq\frac{\gamma_da_y}{2}.
\tag{56}
\]
Since every half-mass witness is pointwise at most one, the sum of the scaled source densities is pointwise at most \(\gamma_d\leq1\).  This proves the source-density assertion after (29).

It remains to prove the capacity certificates.  Fix \(B\in\{\mathrm{eq},\mathrm{neq}\}\).  The definitions give the two identities in (32), and feasibility gives \(\kappa_e^B\leq r_e\).  At a common endpoint \(z\), each contribution is charged to two incident edges, so
\[
 2\beta_z^B
 \leq d_z(r)
 \leq\frac12d_z(q^\times)
 \leq\frac{\gamma_da_z}{2}.
\tag{57}
\]
Both \(x_z\) and \(y_{i,z}\) lie in \(\mathsf M_{a_z/2}(C_z)\), hence each has absolute depth at least \(\gamma_da_z/2\).  Thus the weights \(2\beta_z^B\) are legal selector weights for either point family.  Substituting their total mass \(2P_B\), their base rank, and the minimizing residual ranks from (33) into the selector definition used in accepted fact 179add32aa016da1 proves (34).

Accepted fact 179add32aa016da1 supplies one exact minimum-unmatched centroid host \(\nu_{\mathrm{off}}^{\lambda^\star}\), fixed independently of the cap datum, and proves
\[
 \sum_es_{i,e}\delta_{(m_e,\bar c_e)}
 \leq\nu_{\mathrm{off}}^{\lambda^\star}.
\tag{58}
\]
Since \(\kappa_e^B\leq r_e\leq s_{i,e}\), equations (35)-(36) define a positive submeasure of this same host.  Its intrinsic ranks are exactly (37), so the definition of \(M_{\mathrm{off}}\) used in that accepted fact proves (38).

Fix a midpoint \(m_0\) with \(K_{B,m_0}>0\).  Its source edges have the form
\(\{m_0+v,m_0-v\}\) with \(v\ne0\).  Convexity of \(C\) and positive volume of both endpoint fibers imply \(a_{m_0}>0\).  Moreover, by the computation in accepted fact 179add32aa016da1,
\[
 \kappa_e^B\leq s_{i,e}
 \leq\frac{\gamma_d}{2}
       \min\{a_{m_0+v},a_{m_0-v}\}
 <\gamma_{2d}
       \min\{a_{m_0+v},a_{m_0-v}\}.
\tag{59}
\]
Choose exactly the reflected pairs with \(\kappa_e^B>0\) in the reflected-cloud score.  Their available cloud energy is at least \(K_{B,m_0}\), and their centroid-cloud rank is (39).  This proves (40).

All three capacity bounds are obtained from separate admissible objects.  The proof never replaces their suprema by a common optimizer and never aggregates the local energies (25) or (29).  Thus it yields the stated exact reduction, but no terminal inequality beyond the already separated large-core and affine-retention alternatives.
statement:
Let \(n\geq2\) and \(d\geq1\), let
\(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body, and use all notation and normalizations of accepted facts 179add32aa016da1, 695b44a4f0fdcd3a, dcccecd70b052857, cacf8017a747fd4c, and 1c54f5dc74c15059.  In particular, put
\[
 C_z:=\{x:(z,x)\in C\},\qquad
 a_z:=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z),\qquad
 Z:=\{z\in\mathbb Z^n:a_z>0\},
\]
\[
 W:=\sum_{z\in Z}a_z>0,\qquad
 G:=\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{core}}(C),\qquad
 \gamma_d:=\left(\frac d{d+1}\right)^d,
\]
and, for \(z\in Z\),
\[
 c_z:=\frac1{a_z}\int_{C_z}x\,dx,\qquad
 \mathcal K_z:=\mathsf M_{a_z/2}(C_z),\qquad
 D_z:=\mathcal K_z-c_z.
\tag{1}
\]
Assume, for some \(0<\eta\leq1/4\), that
\[
 G<\frac W4,
 \qquad
 R_{\mathrm{cap}}(C)\leq(1-\eta)W.
\tag{2}
\]
Accepted fact 179add32aa016da1 gives either
\[
 G\geq\frac{\eta^2}{100}W,
\tag{3}
\]
or its synchronized alternative.  Work in the latter alternative, so
\[
 G<\frac{\eta^2}{100}W.
\tag{4}
\]
Fix arbitrarily one saturated-circuit datum
\((p,m,\mathcal Q,i)\in\mathscr H_{\mathrm{sat}}(C)\), including one valid choice of its exact affine minorants and one cap label \(i\).  Let \(w_i\ne0\), \(\ell_i\), and \(\phi_{i,z}\in[0,1]\) be its cap normal, affine minorant, and soft contact factors.

For every parity class \(\xi\), put
\[
 A_\xi:=\sum_{z\equiv\xi\ ({\rm mod}\ 2)}a_z,
 \qquad
 M_\xi:=\max_{z\equiv\xi\ ({\rm mod}\ 2)}a_z,
\]
with \(M_\xi:=0\) for an empty class, and set
and set
\[
 \mathcal G:=\{\xi:A_\xi>0,\ M_\xi\leq A_\xi/4\}.
\tag{5}
\]
Define the strong canonical product matching
\[
 q^\times_{\{u,v\}}
 :=\frac{\gamma_da_ua_v}{A_\xi}
 \quad
 (u\ne v,\ u\equiv v\equiv\xi\ ({\rm mod}\ 2),\ A_\xi>0),
\tag{6}
\]
and define the cap-synchronized soft weights
\[
 s_{i,\{u,v\}}:=
 \begin{cases}
 \frac12q^\times_{\{u,v\}}\phi_{i,u}\phi_{i,v},
 &u,v\text{ lie in a class }\xi\in\mathcal G,\\
 0,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\tag{7}
\]
Choose once a primal optimizer and a gauge-load-minimal dual optimizer
\(v^\times=(v_e^\times)\) for \(q^\times\), as in accepted fact 695b44a4f0fdcd3a, and put
\[
 \omega_e:=h_{D_e}(v_e^\times),\qquad
 D_e:=\frac{D_u+D_v}{2}\quad(e=\{u,v\}).
\tag{8}
\]
In the positive-load case, retain the endpoint loads, normalized directions, and support contacts \(\lambda_{e,z},u_{e,z},x_{e,z}\) associated with this optimizer in the same accepted normalization.
Let \(\mathcal I^\times\) be the same-body interaction of this stress, in the normalization of accepted facts dcccecd70b052857 and cacf8017a747fd4c.  Assume
\[
 \mathcal I^\times=0.
\tag{9}
\]
Define the positive-overlap submatching
\[
 r_e:=\min\{s_{i,e},\omega_e\},
 \qquad
 R:=\sum_er_e,
\tag{10}
\]
and assume the positive-overlap branch
\[
 R>\delta W,
 \qquad
 \delta:=\frac{\gamma_d\eta^2}{16}.
\tag{11}
\]
This is the positive-overlap branch singled out by accepted fact 695b44a4f0fdcd3a; its affine-retention conclusion already applies whenever the complementary clipped residual is macroscopic.

For an edge \(e=\{z,a\}\) and its endpoint \(z\), put
\[
 h_{e,z}:=\frac{a-z}{2}\in\mathbb Z^n.
\tag{12}
\]
Let \(\mathcal A_2(r)\) be the family of unordered pairs \(\{e,f\}\) of distinct positive \(r\)-edges which have a unique common endpoint \(z\) and for which \(h_{e,z},h_{f,z}\) are linearly independent.  Let \(\vartheta\) maximize
\[
 P:=\sum_{\{e,f\}\in\mathcal A_2(r)}\vartheta_{\{e,f\}}
\tag{13}
\]
subject to
\[
 \vartheta_{\{e,f\}}\geq0,
 \qquad
 \sum_{f:\{e,f\}\in\mathcal A_2(r)}
 \vartheta_{\{e,f\}}\leq r_e
 \quad(e:r_e>0).
\tag{14}
\]
Then an optimizer exists and
\[
 \boxed{
 P\geq\frac{R-G}{2},\qquad
 P>\left(\frac12-\frac{2e}{25}\right)R,\qquad
 P>\frac{25\gamma_d-4}{800}\,\eta^2W.}
\tag{15}
\]
In particular, the last coefficient is at least
\((25/e-4)/800>0\), independently of \(n,d\).

Every loaded endpoint \(z\) has, by (9) and accepted fact dcccecd70b052857, a common stress contact \(x_z\in\mathcal K_z\) and a common normalized stress direction \(u_z\ne0\) for all loaded stress edges incident with \(z\).  Put
\[
 \rho_{i,z}:=h_{D_z}(w_i)>0,
 \qquad
 \widehat w_{i,z}:=\frac{w_i}{\rho_{i,z}},
\tag{16}
\]
and let \(y_{i,z}\in\mathcal K_z\) be the unique support contact in direction \(w_i\).  Thus
\[
 h_{D_z}(u_z)=h_{D_z}(\widehat w_{i,z})=1,
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 x_z=y_{i,z}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 u_z=\widehat w_{i,z}.}
\tag{17}
\]
For a contribution \(\sigma=(z;e,f)\) with
\(\theta_\sigma:=\vartheta_{\{e,f\}}>0\), classify \(\sigma\) as equal-contact when \(x_z=y_{i,z}\), and as distinct-contact otherwise.  Let
\[
 P_{\mathrm{eq}}:=\sum_{\sigma:\,x_z=y_{i,z}}\theta_\sigma,
 \qquad
 P_{\mathrm{neq}}:=\sum_{\sigma:\,x_z\ne y_{i,z}}\theta_\sigma.
\tag{18}
\]
Then
\[
 P_{\mathrm{eq}}+P_{\mathrm{neq}}=P,
 \qquad
 \boxed{
 \max\{P_{\mathrm{eq}},P_{\mathrm{neq}}\}
 \geq\frac P2,\qquad
 \max\{P_{\mathrm{eq}},P_{\mathrm{neq}}\}
 >\left(\frac14-\frac e{25}\right)R,\qquad
 \max\{P_{\mathrm{eq}},P_{\mathrm{neq}}\}
 >\frac{25\gamma_d-4}{1600}\,\eta^2W.}
\tag{19}
\]

The two classes have the following exact geometric meanings.  Orient one contribution as
\[
 e=\{z,a\},\qquad f=\{z,b\},
 \qquad
 \Phi_\sigma(s,t):=z+s\frac{a-z}{2}+t\frac{b-z}{2}.
\tag{20}
\]
The chart \(\Phi_\sigma\) is an integral affine injection of rank two.

(a) For every equal-contact contribution, let \(x_{e,a}\) and \(x_{f,b}\) be the stress support contacts at the opposite endpoints.  The four points
\[
 X_{00}:=x_z,
 \quad
 X_{10}:=\frac{x_z+x_{e,a}}2,
 \quad
 X_{01}:=\frac{x_z+x_{f,b}}2,
 \quad
 X_{11}:=\frac{x_{e,a}+x_{f,b}}2
\tag{21}
\]
satisfy
\[
 X_{jk}\in\mathsf M_{\theta_\sigma}
       (C_{\Phi_\sigma(j,k)})
 \quad(j,k\in\{0,1\}),
\tag{22}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{X_{00}-X_{10}-X_{01}+X_{11}=0.}
\tag{23}
\]
Moreover, equality at \(z\) propagates across \(e\) and \(f\):
\[
 x_{e,a}=y_{i,a},\qquad x_{f,b}=y_{i,b}.
\tag{24}
\]
Thus (21) is a cap-aligned affine stress-square germ.  Every corner has absolute fiber depth at least \(\gamma_d\theta_\sigma\), and its legal rank-two local packet has energy
\[
 \mathcal E_\sigma=4\gamma_d\theta_\sigma.
\tag{25}
\]

(b) For every distinct-contact contribution, define the cap-versus-stress four-corner array
\[
 Y_{00}:=x_z,
 \quad
 Y_{10}:=\frac{x_z+x_{e,a}}2,
 \quad
 Y_{01}:=\frac{y_{i,z}+y_{i,b}}2,
 \quad
 Y_{11}:=\frac{x_{e,a}+y_{i,b}}2.
\tag{26}
\]
Then
\[
 Y_{jk}\in\mathsf M_{\theta_\sigma}
       (C_{\Phi_\sigma(j,k)})
 \quad(j,k\in\{0,1\}),
\tag{27}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 Y_{00}-Y_{10}-Y_{01}+Y_{11}
 =\frac{x_z-y_{i,z}}2\ne0.}
\tag{28}
\]
Hence this is a genuine nonseparable native rank-two cap-versus-stress atlas atom.  Again every corner has depth at least \(\gamma_d\theta_\sigma\), and its legal local packet has energy
\[
 \mathcal E_\sigma=4\gamma_d\theta_\sigma.
\tag{29}
\]
For the outer points \(X_{11}\) in (a), respectively \(Y_{11}\) in (b), the entire labeled family admits simultaneous source-fiber densities: for every subfamily and every physical source fiber, the sum of the source densities is pointwise at most \(\gamma_d\leq1\).  This is only a source-density assertion; it does not add independently produced densities in a common target fiber.

There are also exact branchwise capacity certificates.  For
\(B\in\{\mathrm{eq},\mathrm{neq}\}\), define
\[
 \beta_z^B:=
 \sum_{\substack{\sigma=(z;e,f)\text{ of type }B}}
 \theta_\sigma,
 \qquad
 E_B:=\{z:\beta_z^B>0\},
\tag{30}
\]
and
\[
 \kappa_e^B:=
 \sum_{\substack{\sigma=(z;e_\sigma,f_\sigma)\text{ of type }B\\
                   e\in\{e_\sigma,f_\sigma\}}}
 \theta_\sigma.
\tag{31}
\]
Thus every contribution is charged once to each of its two source edges.  One has the exact identities and bounds
\[
 \sum_z2\beta_z^B=2P_B,
 \qquad
 \sum_e\kappa_e^B=2P_B,
 \qquad
 0\leq\kappa_e^B\leq r_e\leq s_{i,e}.
\tag{32}
\]
If \(P_B>0\), put
\[
 \rho_B^{\mathrm{end}}:=\dim\operatorname{aff}(E_B),
\]
\[
 r_{B,x}:=\min_{s\text{ affine}}
 \dim\operatorname{span}\{x_z-s(z):z\in E_B\},
 \qquad
 r_{B,y}:=\min_{s\text{ affine}}
 \dim\operatorname{span}\{y_{i,z}-s(z):z\in E_B\},
\tag{33}
\]
where the minima range over affine maps from \(\operatorname{aff}(E_B)\) to \(\mathbb R^d\).  Then the residual-selector capacity from accepted fact 179add32aa016da1 obeys the two separate certificates
\[
 \boxed{
 R_{\mathrm{sel}}(C)
 \geq2^{n-\rho_B^{\mathrm{end}}}
       \frac{2P_B}{r_{B,x}+1},
 \qquad
 R_{\mathrm{sel}}(C)
 \geq2^{n-\rho_B^{\mathrm{end}}}
       \frac{2P_B}{r_{B,y}+1}.}
\tag{34}
\]
For the equal-contact type, the two point families and the two certificates coincide.

For \(e=\{u,v\}\), put
\[
 m_e:=\frac{u+v}{2},
 \qquad
 \bar c_e:=\frac{c_u+c_v}{2},
\]
and define the source-edge centroid measure, with coincident atoms aggregated, by
\[
 \Sigma_B^{\mathrm{src}}
 :=\sum_e\kappa_e^B\delta_{(m_e,\bar c_e)}.
\tag{35}
\]
This is a positive submeasure of the single fixed exact host
\(\nu_{\mathrm{off}}^{\lambda^\star}\) from accepted fact 179add32aa016da1, and
\[
 |\Sigma_B^{\mathrm{src}}|=2P_B.
\tag{36}
\]
Put
\[
 \rho_B^{\mathrm{src}}
 :=\dim\operatorname{aff}
 \operatorname{proj}_{\mathbb R^n}
 (\operatorname{supp}\Sigma_B^{\mathrm{src}}),
\]
\[
 r_B^{\mathrm{src}}
 :=\dim\operatorname{aff}
 (\operatorname{supp}\Sigma_B^{\mathrm{src}})
 -\rho_B^{\mathrm{src}}.
\tag{37}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 M_{\mathrm{off}}(C)
 \geq2^{n-\rho_B^{\mathrm{src}}}
       \frac{2P_B}{r_B^{\mathrm{src}}+1}.}
\tag{38}
\]

Finally, for an integral midpoint \(m_0\), let
\[
 K_{B,m_0}:=
 \sum_{e:m_e=m_0}\kappa_e^B,
 \qquad
 r_{B,m_0}^{\mathrm{cloud}}
 :=\dim\operatorname{aff}
 \{\bar c_e:\kappa_e^B>0,\ m_e=m_0\}.
\tag{39}
\]
Whenever \(K_{B,m_0}>0\), one has \(m_0\in Z\) and
\[
 \boxed{
 R_{\mathrm{cloud}}(C)
 \geq2^n\frac{K_{B,m_0}}
                 {r_{B,m_0}^{\mathrm{cloud}}+1}.}
\tag{40}
\]
The measures and scores in (34), (38), and (40) are separate certificates.  They are not asserted to be simultaneously attained by one mixed center.  Likewise, (25) and (29) are atomwise packet energies only: no sum of energies over distinct or incompatible charts is claimed.
